q: בן 72, נשוי 2+, ארכיטקט שפרש לגמלאות לפני שנתיים. ללא רקע רפואי רלוונטי, אינו נוטל תרופות. מגיע להערכה גריאטרית בשל ירידה תפקודית מזה חצי שנה. לדברי המשפחה יש ימים שהוא "מפוזר", לא מגיע לפגישות. לפני כחודש המשטרה עצרה אותו נוסע נגד כיוון התנועה בכביש חד סטרי רחוק ממקום מגוריו והוא הגיב באגרסיביות. מאז בטוח שהמשטרה עוקבת אחריו, ואומר שרואה שוטרים בביתו מסתובבים בלילה. בנוסף אשתו מספרת על הפרעות בשינה, בשנים האחרונות צועק ובועט בזמן השינה. המשפחה מדווחת שיש ימים שהמטופל מתפקד רגיל ואף עוזר לבנו בעסק המשפחתי. המטופל מדווח על מצב רוח ירוד מאז היציאה לפנסיה ואומר שמרגיש שאין טעם לחייו. מספר שמרגיש שגורר רגליים בהליכה ונפל 4 פעמים בחצי שנה אחרונה. בבדיקת MOCA ציון 19. זיכרון 5/3 מילים, תפקודים ניהוליים וקשב לקויים מאוד. מה מהבאים מהווה CORE FEATURE לאבחנה של מצבו?
o: דלוזיות פרנואידליות
נפילות חוזרות
דיכאון
פלוקטואציות במצב הקוגניטיבי
explanation:
**Fluctuating cognition**, with prominent variations in attention and alertness, is a core feature of DLB. The executive and attentional deficits and variable functioning in the case fit this pattern; Table 63-3 distinguishes core features from supportive findings (p. 984).

**A. Paranoid delusions.** Wrong, systematized delusions are supportive; recurrent visual hallucinations are core features. The two symptoms should not be conflated (p. 984).
**B. Repeated falls.** Wrong, these are supportive rather than core features, even when prominent in the history (p. 984).
**C. Depression.** Wrong, depression is supportive; its presence does not make it the core criterion requested (p. 984).
**D. Fluctuations in cognitive status.** Correct, fluctuating cognition with marked variations in attention and alertness is explicitly a core feature and fits the differing days of function in the stem (p. 984).
Source: Hazzard 8e, p. 984, Table 63-3.

q: An ambulant older adult has chronic constipation and can drink adequate fluids. There is no fecal impaction or rectal evacuation disorder. Which initial medication regimen follows Table 87-11 in Hazzard?
o: Give senna together with lactulose as the starting daily regimen
Give psyllium with adequate fluids as the starting daily regimen
Give daily oil-retention enemas as the starting evacuation regimen
Give regular glycerin suppositories as the starting evacuation regimen
explanation:
A **bulk laxative** is the starting point in the table for ambulant older people with adequate fluid intake. The stepwise approach separates uncomplicated chronic constipation from high-risk patients, impaction, and rectal outlet delay (p. 1378).
"Bulk laxative (psyllium) 1–3 times daily with fluids as required" (p. 1378).
"Senna 2–3 tablets at bedtime and sorbitol or lactulose 30 mL daily, titrating upward as needed" (p. 1378).

**A. Give senna together with lactulose as the starting daily regimen.** Wrong, the table places the senna-plus-lactulose regimen in the high-risk pathway, rather than as the starting step for this ambulant patient (p. 1378).
**B. Give psyllium with adequate fluids as the starting daily regimen.** Correct, psyllium with fluids is the initial regimen in the ambulant chronic-constipation pathway (p. 1378).
**C. Give daily oil-retention enemas as the starting evacuation regimen.** Wrong, oil-retention enemas belong to the impaction-with-obstruction pathway, which the stem does not describe (p. 1378).
**D. Give regular glycerin suppositories as the starting evacuation regimen.** Wrong, regular glycerin suppositories belong to the rectal-outlet-delay pathway, not the starting step specified here (p. 1378).

Source: Hazzard’s Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8e, pp. 1378.
label: Source: Hazzard 8e (marked) · p. 1378, Table 87-11

q: What explains the USPSTF position on routine screening for thyroid dysfunction in adults as presented in Hazzard?
o: Clinical trials provide insufficient evidence for treating subclinical thyroid dysfunction.
Controlled trials demonstrate excess harm from treating overt thyroid dysfunction.
TSH measurement is not readily available for assessing suspected thyroid dysfunction.
Subclinical thyroid dysfunction is less common than overt thyroid disease in older adults.
explanation:
**Screening requires evidence about management of the abnormalities detected.** Hazzard states that subclinical dysfunction is more common than overt disease but is not sufficiently supported by clinical trial data for its management; it presents the USPSTF conclusion as insufficient evidence to recommend routine screening (p. 1554). "the management of subclinical thyroid dysfunction, which is more common than overt disease, is not sufficiently supported by clinical trial data." (p. 1554).

**A. Clinical trials provide insufficient evidence for treating subclinical thyroid dysfunction.** Correct, this is the source’s stated limitation: uncertainty about management of subclinical disease prevents a firm evidentiary basis for routine screening (p. 1554).
**B. Controlled trials demonstrate excess harm from treating overt thyroid dysfunction.** Wrong, the source describes the adverse effects of overt hypo- and hyperthyroidism as reversible with treatment, not as a demonstrated excess harm from treating overt disease (p. 1553).
**C. TSH measurement is not readily available for assessing suspected thyroid dysfunction.** Wrong, Hazzard explicitly describes TSH as readily available, so lack of availability is not the reason for the screening position (p. 1554).
**D. Subclinical thyroid dysfunction is less common than overt thyroid disease in older adults.** Wrong, the source states that subclinical dysfunction is more common than overt disease, making this proposed explanation incorrect (p. 1554).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 1554, 1553.
ref: Hazzard Ch 98 — THYROID DISEASES · Harrison Ch 388 — Approach to the Patient with Endocrine Disorders

o: רעש נשימתי מהצטברות הפרשות בדרכי אוויר בחולה גוסס; טיפול: Hyoscine (Scopolamine) או Glycopyrrolate
סימן לדלקת ריאות הדורש אנטיביוטיקה
סימן לאסתמה
סימן לכשל לבבי חריף
explanation:
**Death rattle מתרחש ב-23-92% מהגוססים**.

**א. רעש נשימתי מהצטברות הפרשות בדרכי אוויר בחולה גוסס; טיפול: Hyoscine (Scopolamine) או Glycopyrrolate.** נכונה, נגרם מחוסר יכולת לפנות הפרשות. Anticholinergics (Hyoscine butylbromide 20mg SC, Glycopyrrolate 0.2mg SC) מפחיתים ייצור הפרשות. שאיבה לא מומלצת — גורמת אי-נוחות. חשוב להסביר למשפחה שהמטופל אינו סובל.
**ב. סימן לדלקת ריאות הדורש אנטיביוטיקה.** שגויה.
**ג. סימן לאסתמה.** שגויה.
**ד. סימן לכשל לבבי חריף.** שגויה.

q: An 82-year-old man had a stroke six months ago and has mild residual left-sided weakness and fear of falling. He wants to improve strength and balance but worries about his limitations. His wife is supportive and also concerned about safety. Which program design follows the adherence strategies described by Hazzard?
o: Rapid increases in training intensity, emphasizing early strength gains
Flexible patient-set goals, family support, and personalized feedback
Fixed distance targets, emphasizing strict attainment at each session
Independent exercise sessions, avoiding family involvement in planning
explanation:
**Exercise adherence** is supported by gradual progression, personalized feedback, family involvement, and goals set by the participant. These strategies address continuation of the program as well as its exercise content (p. 814). The source recommends "flexible goals (time rather than distance) set by the participant" (p. 814).

**A. Rapid increases in training intensity, emphasizing early strength gains.** Wrong, rapid escalation conflicts with the source recommendation for slow progression to reduce early injuries (p. 814).
**B. Flexible patient-set goals, family support, and personalized feedback.** Correct, this combines the participant-set goals, family support, and individualized feedback explicitly described to reduce dropout (p. 814).
**C. Fixed distance targets, emphasizing strict attainment at each session.** Wrong, fixed distance targets do not follow the recommended flexible, time-based goals chosen by the participant (p. 814).
**D. Independent exercise sessions, avoiding family involvement in planning.** Wrong, excluding family involvement removes a source of support specifically recommended for participation (p. 814).

Source: Hazzard, 8th edition, pp. 814.

q: An 86-year-old woman with heart failure and congestion is receiving a loop diuretic. After treatment adjustment her congestion improves and creatinine rises slightly. Which monitoring principle follows Hazzard?
o: Reduce diuresis for the creatinine rise despite persistent congestion
Assess volume status and electrolytes alongside the creatinine change
Use the creatinine change as the measure of fluid removal
Add metolazone to reduce the need for electrolyte monitoring
explanation:
**Creatinine changes must be interpreted with volume status.** Diuresis can resolve hemodilution and raise measured creatinine, while overdiuresis can also cause kidney injury; the rise therefore needs clinical interpretation (p. 1182). "For this reason, electrolytes should be monitored closely when diuretic therapy is being adjusted." (p. 1182).

**A. Reduce diuresis for the creatinine rise despite persistent congestion.** Wrong, the source warns that accepting persistent congestion to avoid titration can worsen symptoms and other outcomes; a creatinine rise alone does not settle the volume assessment (p. 1182).
**B. Assess volume status and electrolytes alongside the creatinine change.** Correct, this incorporates congestion, possible hypovolemia, and electrolyte effects into interpretation of creatinine (p. 1182).
**C. Use the creatinine change as the measure of fluid removal.** Wrong, the source describes a complex relationship influenced by hemodilution and perfusion, not a direct fluid-removal measurement (p. 1182).
**D. Add metolazone to reduce the need for electrolyte monitoring.** Wrong, metolazone requires particular monitoring because it can cause a brisk response and serious electrolyte disturbances (p. 1182).

Source: Hazzard, 8th edition, pp. 1182.

q: A woman with symptomatic knee osteoarthritis has not yet tried an anti-inflammatory medication and wants topical treatment before an oral drug. Which rationale supports topical diclofenac according to Hazzard?
o: Deep penetration that makes it particularly suitable for hip osteoarthritis
Broad systemic action that makes it suited to many affected joints
Pain relief with a favorable adverse-effect profile
Cartilage modification that replaces the need for symptom treatment
explanation:
**Topical NSAIDs** are recommended before oral NSAIDs for hand and knee osteoarthritis because of their efficacy for pain and favorable adverse-effect profile. Limited penetration makes the hip a different situation, and many affected joints may favor systemic therapy (p. 787). The source cites their "favorable side effect profile and efficacy of pain relief." (p. 787).

**A. Deep penetration that makes it particularly suitable for hip osteoarthritis.** Wrong, hip joint depth limits topical NSAID efficacy; the source does not recommend them for hip osteoarthritis on the proposed penetration rationale (p. 787).
**B. Broad systemic action that makes it suited to many affected joints.** Wrong, a large number of affected joints makes topical therapy less ideal, with systemic therapy preferred in that setting (p. 787).
**C. Pain relief with a favorable adverse-effect profile.** Correct, pain relief and the favorable adverse-effect profile are the stated reasons for using topical NSAIDs before oral therapy in knee osteoarthritis (p. 787).
**D. Cartilage modification that replaces the need for symptom treatment.** Wrong, disease-modifying osteoarthritis drugs are described as unavailable; topical diclofenac is presented for symptom relief, not as a cartilage-modifying replacement (pp. 787–788).

Source: Hazzard, 8th edition, pp. 787, 788.
ref: Hazzard Ch 68 — PAIN MANAGEMENT· Harrison Ch 436 — Seizures and Epilepsy

q: אישה עם ירידה קוגניטיבית קלה יכולה להבין ולקבל החלטות בנוגע לענייניה כאשר המידע מונגש לה. נשקלת קבלת החלטות נתמכת בישראל. מהו תפקיד התומך?
o: לקבל החלטות במקומה לאחר שמיעת העדפותיה
לסייע לה לבטא ולממש את החלטותיה
להעביר את ההחלטות לבת לאחר בירור רצונותיה
לבחור עבורה מסגרת מגורים בהתאם להמלצה רפואית
explanation:
**קבלת החלטות נתמכת** מיועדת לבגיר שיכול להחליט בעצמו בעזרת תמיכה. התומך מסייע בביטוי הרצון ובמימוש ההחלטות, אך אינו מחליט בשם האדם; כך נשמרת ההבחנה בין סיוע בהחלטה להחלפת מקבל ההחלטה (סעיף 67ב, עמ׳ 62).
"תומך בקבלת החלטות לא יקבל החלטות בשמו של האדם שהוא מסייע לו." (עמ׳ 62).

**א. לקבל החלטות במקומה לאחר שמיעת העדפותיה.** שגויה, שמיעת העדפות אינה מתירה לתומך להחליף את האדם בקבלת ההחלטה (עמ׳ 62).
**ב. לסייע לה לבטא ולממש את החלטותיה.** נכונה, הסיוע מתייחס להחלטותיה שלה, בהתאם לתפקיד שקובע החוק (עמ׳ 62).
**ג. להעביר את ההחלטות לבת לאחר בירור רצונותיה.** שגויה, העברת ההחלטה לבת אינה הסיוע בקבלת החלטות עצמאית שהחוק מתאר (עמ׳ 62).
**ד. לבחור עבורה מסגרת מגורים בהתאם להמלצה רפואית.** שגויה, בחירה עבור האדם מחליפה את החלטתו, במקום לתמוך בה (עמ׳ 62).

מקור: חוק הכשרות המשפטית והאפוטרופסות, סעיף 67ב, עמ׳ 62.
ref: Hazzard Ch 17 — COMMUNITY-BASED LONG-TERM SERVICES AND SUPPORT, AND HOME-BASED MEDICAL CARE
chapterTitle: COMMUNITY-BASED LONG-TERM SERVICES AND SUPPORT, AND HOME-BASED MEDICAL CARE

q: A man with lower urinary tract symptoms has not improved with empiric treatment. He has low urinary flow and residual urine, but bladder outlet obstruction and impaired detrusor contractility remain possible. Which test is the standard for diagnosing obstruction?
o: Cystoscopic inspection of the bladder outlet
Cystometric pressure measurement during bladder filling
Residual-volume measurement after spontaneous voiding
Pressure-flow measurement during bladder emptying
explanation:
**Pressure-flow testing** measures bladder pressure and flow simultaneously during voiding. Low flow alone is not specific for obstruction because impaired detrusor contractility can also cause it; high pressure with low flow indicates obstruction (p. 562).
"The standard for diagnosing BOO is pressure-flow study, which simultaneously measures flow rate versus bladder pressure during voiding." (p. 562).
"A high bladder pressure combined with a low flow rate is indicative of BOO." (p. 562).

**A. Cystoscopic inspection of the bladder outlet.** Wrong, the source specifically says cystoscopy should not be used to diagnose bladder outlet obstruction (p. 562).
**B. Cystometric pressure measurement during bladder filling.** Wrong, filling cystometry assesses detrusor function during filling rather than the pressure-flow relationship during voiding (p. 562).
**C. Residual-volume measurement after spontaneous voiding.** Wrong, residual volume is not significantly associated with bladder outlet obstruction and does not resolve this distinction (p. 562).
**D. Pressure-flow measurement during bladder emptying.** Correct, simultaneous pressure and flow measurement is the diagnostic standard and distinguishes the high-pressure, low-flow pattern (p. 562).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 562.
ref: Hazzard Ch 47 — INCONTINENCE· Harrison Ch 79 — Infections in Patients with Cancer

q: An 85-year-old nursing home resident with advanced dementia and dysphagia receives thickened liquids. She is less responsive, with sodium 168 mEq/L, BUN 88, creatinine 2.1, and urine specific gravity 1.030. Staff report refusal of thickened water but acceptance of pudding and ice cream. Which mechanism fits the reported intake and a renal concentrating response?
o: Renal water loss accompanied by failure to concentrate the urine
Inadequate water intake accompanied by a concentrated urinary response
Renal water excretion accompanied by appropriately dilute urine in hyponatremia
Preserved water intake accompanied by continued loss of dilute urine
explanation:
**Water deprivation** is a recognized contributor to hypernatremia in dependent older adults (pp. 587-588). Hazzard describes the renal response as "a low-volume, highly concentrated urine" and directs assessment toward inadequate fluid access or extrarenal losses when that response is present (p. 588). Applying that pattern to water refusal and concentrated urine here is an inference, rather than proof that no additional contributor exists.

**A. Renal water loss accompanied by failure to concentrate the urine.** Wrong, Renal water loss from a concentrating defect is associated with polyuria or dilute urine in the source, not the concentrating response asked about (p. 588).
**B. Inadequate water intake accompanied by a concentrated urinary response.** Correct, This connects the observed poor intake with the concentrating response described in hypernatremia (p. 588).
**C. Renal water excretion accompanied by appropriately dilute urine in hyponatremia.** Wrong, The vignette describes hypernatremia and concentrated urine, not the low sodium and dilution described by this option (pp. 587-588).
**D. Preserved water intake accompanied by continued loss of dilute urine.** Wrong, Both preserved intake and dilute urine conflict with the reported water refusal and concentrating response (p. 588).

Source: Hazzard, 8th edition, pp. 587, 588.
ref: Hazzard Ch 31 — DISORDERS OF SWALLOWING · Harrison Ch 50 — Unintentional Weight Loss

q: איזה תפקוד קוגניטיבי צפוי להישמר בהזדקנות תקינה?
o: Speed of information processing
Complex visuospatial skills
Verbal Fluency
Semantic memory
explanation:
In normal aging, **semantic memory**, or general knowledge not tied to a particular event, tends to be preserved. It differs from the speed and complexity of information processing, which can decline; Table 57-1 distinguishes preserved from declining abilities (Hazzard 8e, p. 854).

**A. Speed of information processing.** Wrong, it is listed among functions that decline (p. 854).
**B. Complex visuospatial skills.** Wrong, mental rotation, complex copying and mental assembly decline, unlike simple copying (p. 854).
**C. Verbal fluency.** Wrong, verbal fluency and spontaneous word finding decline even though comprehension and vocabulary remain preserved (p. 854).
**D. Semantic memory.** Correct, semantic recall is explicitly listed among preserved memory functions (p. 854).

Source: Hazzard 8e, p. 854, Table 57-1.
chapterTitle: SEXUALITY , SEXUAL FUNCTION, AND THE AGING MAN

q: After prolonged pressure over a bony prominence, an older adult’s skin is still intact. Which interpretation best reflects the tissue injury process described by Hazzard?
o: Pressure-related muscle damage can precede visible injury to the overlying skin.
Ischemic muscle can resist tissue deformation better than adequately oxygenated muscle.
Local inflammatory edema can improve arteriolar circulation in the injured tissue.
Reperfusion can protect the endothelium by reducing oxygen-free radical release.
explanation:
**Deep tissue injury can precede visible skin breakdown** because pressure deforms tissues and compromises their circulation. Muscle may sustain irreversible damage while the overlying skin has not yet shown such damage; inflammatory edema can remain clinically invisible for 2 to 7 days (p. 681).
"irreversible damage may be present at the muscle layer without such damage occurring in the skin or subcutaneous layers." (p. 681).
"These inflammatory changes with tissue edema can occur from 2 to 7 days before visible skin breakdown." (p. 681).

**A. Pressure-related muscle damage can precede visible injury to the overlying skin.** Correct, The page describes irreversible muscle injury without corresponding skin injury; intact-looking skin therefore does not exclude deeper damage (p. 681).
**B. Ischemic muscle can resist tissue deformation better than adequately oxygenated muscle.** Wrong, The source identifies ischemic muscle as more sensitive to deformation, so oxygen deprivation increases vulnerability rather than improving resistance (p. 681).
**C. Local inflammatory edema can improve arteriolar circulation in the injured tissue.** Wrong, Inflammation raises interstitial pressure and further impedes arteriolar flow; edema therefore worsens the circulation supporting the injured tissue (p. 681).
**D. Reperfusion can protect the endothelium by reducing oxygen-free radical release.** Wrong, Reoxygenation releases oxygen-free radicals that cause new endothelial injury; the proposed reduction in radical release misidentifies the reperfusion mechanism (p. 681).

Source: Hazzard’s Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8e, pp. 681.
